script:
Japanese students can party all night without stepping inside a nightclub.

After midnight, some university students book a private karaoke room instead of entering a nightclub. The box gives them one place to stay, sing, and talk.

They order noodles and soft drinks from the room phone, then trade songs. Friends grab microphones one after another, while lyrics flash across the dark room. The party stays loud, but the room keeps it private.

Near sunrise, one student sings while another dozes on the sofa. This is asa-kara, or morning karaoke, turning the end of a night out into its own event.
